reason: Membrane fats appear to form the boundary that can enclose the cell fluid.
expectation: The fats will surround the fluid to begin forming a cell boundary.

effect: The fats enclosed the fluid, but the boundary still lacks protein channels.
reaction: The picture makes the missing channels clear.
reason: Transport proteins appear to add channels to the membrane and help make the boundary selective.
expectation: The transport proteins will fit into the membrane, creating a selective boundary.

effect: The selective boundary is complete, and the cell model now needs stored instructions and ATP machinery.
reaction: The picture clearly connects protein channels with selective transport.
reason: DNA contains the stored instructions, and nuclear envelopes appear to hold it in nuclei.
expectation: The DNA will be enclosed in nuclei for the muscle-cell model.

effect: The DNA and nuclear envelopes formed muscle nuclei, which appear ready to supply the cell model's stored instructions.
reaction: The porous envelopes connect well with the earlier explanation that RNA can leave the nucleus.
reason: The muscle nuclei appear to fit the model's stored-instructions slot.
expectation: The nuclei will be installed as the cell model's stored instructions.

effect: The nuclei are installed in the muscle-cell model; the ATP machinery is still needed.
reaction: The inset reinforces how copied instructions can leave the nuclei.
reason: Mitochondria appear to fit the oxygen-using ATP machinery slot.
expectation: The mitochondria will be installed as the cell model's ATP machinery.

effect: The mitochondria are installed, and the next goal is to make pulling proteins and structures. The correction indicates that the installed nuclei are no longer selectable separately.
reaction: The fuel and oxygen diagram makes the mitochondria's role clearer.
reason: The RNA building blocks use DNA as a template, and the DNA is now inside the cell model.
expectation: The building blocks will use the installed DNA to make an RNA copy of the instructions.

alternatives.reason: I could check their available partners if the installed nuclei cannot be reached through the model.

effect: The cell model's DNA produced an RNA copy that can reach a ribosome; the DNA remains in the nucleus.
reaction: The picture makes the copy's journey clear.
reason: The copied instructions are headed toward a ribosome, which makes proteins.
expectation: The ribosomes will use the copied instructions to make muscle pulling proteins.

effect: The ribosomes used the copied instructions to make pulling protein threads, while the RNA and ribosomes remain intact.
reaction: The two panels help connect protein production with the organized threads.
reason: The cell model needs pulling structures, so the new protein threads appear ready to be added.
expectation: The threads will give the muscle-cell model its pulling structures.

effect: The protein threads completed the muscle fibers. The final picture shows how greater filament overlap shortens a repeating unit without shortening the filaments themselves.
reaction: The two poses made me curious about how the filaments move past each other.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the RNA copy was most worthwhile because the picture connected DNA staying in the nucleus with instructions reaching ribosomes outside it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the nuclei was a predictable fitting step, although its inset reinforced the RNA journey.

surprise.text: The final picture showed that the repeating unit shortens while the individual filaments keep their length.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the goals, item names and picture descriptions gave me a reason for each combination.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the muscle fibers become tissue and connect to other body systems. Building from instructions to pulling structures gave me a reason to be curious about that next scale.
